reason: Both conversations get the critical safety sequence right: stay off the wet floor, switch off at the consumer unit from a dry spot, then turn off the water. Conversation 2 then moves toward the real cause. It guides look-only checks, has her find the split door seal and the trapped underwire, correctly names the seal as the likely cause, advises against taping or gluing it, and recommends an engineer plus an electrician for the socket. Conversation 1 never finds the leak. It sends her to drain the machine through the filter, which spills even more water near the socket and checks the wrong things, and it suggests unplugging the machine and switching the main back on with only the kitchen circuit off. Conversation 2 has some garbled formatting and overstates the socket as certainly wet, but it is more accurate, better targeted and better escalated overall.
